routine: C0/93E1-9922 — player "move-step executor": screen/camera-coordinate integration + tilemap-strip-redraw scheduler (the back half of the C0/881E player controller body). NOT the WRAM-position/collision core.
summary: This cluster is the per-frame executor that consumes the whole-pixel step counts $1D41-$1D4C produced by C0/91AC/9300 (which decode the 8.4 fractional velocity accumulators $1D3B-$1D40 into +/- per-direction integer pixel counts) and applies them ONE PIXEL AT A TIME by INC/DEC-ing six pairs of screen/camera coordinate bytes ($1D0A/$1D0C, $1D0E/$1D10, $1D12/$1D14, $1D16/$1D18) and their wrap phase-counters ($1D93-$1D98) plus tile-ring indices ($1D87/$1D89/$1D8B/$1D8D/$1D8F/$1D91). When a coordinate phase counter wraps a tile boundary (==0x0F/0x07/0x1F/0x0F or 0/0x08/0x10) it sets bits in scratch redraw-request bytes $1D74-$1D7B and increments the VRAM ring position; the trailing routines (979B/97CC/97FD/982E/985F/9890/98C1/98F2) then test those bits and JSR the background-strip/VRAM-column builders at C0/8243-8425 (which write WMADDL/H $2181/$2183 and call the strip builders $7612/$79CF/$7D66/$77E4/$7BA9/$7E60), advancing ring buffers $1D99-$1D9E (mod 0x3F/0x1F). It ends BRL C0/7F9A which finalizes the VRAM tilemap-strip descriptors. CRITICAL FINDING (trace-verified on disasm/boot_trace_play.txt at line 660+): this tree NEVER calls the collision core 9C5C, the prop-fetch 9AA1/9AC8, or 9D54, and never touches the player world position $1D62/$1D64 — in the captured frame every walker took its early RTS (step counts all 0). So the prompt's hypothesis that 93E1 is "position-integration + collision-apply" is REFUTED: 93E1 is the camera-scroll / sprite-screen-coord / tile-redraw integrator. The actual $1D62/$1D64+collision (9C5C, 9AA1) lives in a different sub-path that did not execute in this stationary-frame trace and must be located separately.
dp: $1D00 (D = $1D00, set by LDA #$1D00; TCD at C0/881E and C0/9DE1; so every "$XX" dp operand = $7E:1DXX). The BRL-target finalizer C0/7F9A also runs under D=$1D00. Sub-effect routines C0/8243-8425 run under the same D=$1D00.
cPseudocode:
/* ============================================================================
 * C0/93E1  moveStepExecutor()  -- DP = $1D00.  All v.NN are WRAM $7E1DNN.
 * Inputs (produced by C0/91AC + C0/9300 earlier in the C0/881E body):
 *   v.41 = -X whole-pixel step count   v.42 = +X step count   (X axis, layer A)
 *   v.43 = -Y / v.44 = +Y              (Y axis, layer A)
 *   v.45 = -X / v.46 = +X              (layer B)   v.47/v.48 = -Y/+Y (layer B)
 *   v.49 = -X / v.4A = +X              (layer C)   v.4B/v.4C = -Y/+Y (layer C)
 *   (each is 0..15; exactly one of each +/- pair is nonzero per 91AC split)
 * v.0BC9 (abs $0BC9) selects scroll/redraw ordering: BPL=normal, BMI=alt.
 * v.35 = per-frame "already-requested this edge" flag set (bits 1/2/4 per axis-effect).
 * ==========================================================================*/
void moveStepExecutor(void)                 /* 93E1 */
{
    v.76 = v.77 = v.74 = v.75 = 0;          /* 93E1-93E7 clear redraw-request scratch */

    stepXpos();                             /* 93E9 JSR 944B : apply +X steps (v.42) */
    stepXneg();                             /* 93EC JSR 947D : apply -X steps (v.41) */
    stepYpos();                             /* 93EF JSR 94DF : apply +Y steps (v.43) */
    stepYneg();                             /* 93F2 JSR 94AD : apply -Y steps (v.44) */

    if ((int8_t)v.0BC9 >= 0) {              /* 93F5 LDA $0BC9; BPL  -> normal order */
        stepB_46(); /*950F*/  stepB_45(); /*9545*/  stepB_47(); /*95AF*/  stepB_48(); /*9579*/
    } else {                                /* 9408 alt order (wider thresholds) */
        stepB_46alt(); /*95E3*/ stepB_45alt(); /*9619*/ stepB_47alt(); /*9683*/ stepB_48alt(); /*964D*/
    }                                       /* 9414 */
    stepC_4A(); /*96B7*/ stepC_49(); /*96ED*/ stepC_4B(); /*975F*/ stepC_4C(); /*9721*/

    v.78 = v.79 = v.7A = v.7B = 0;          /* 9420-9426 clear strip-built flags */

    if ((int8_t)v.0BC9 >= 0) {              /* 9428 BPL */
        redrawA_pos(); /*98C1*/ redrawA_neg(); /*985F*/ redrawB_pos(); /*97FD*/ redrawB_neg(); /*979B*/
        goto done;                          /* 9439 BRL 7F9A */
    } else {                                /* 943C */
        redrawA_negB();/*98F2*/ redrawA_posB();/*9890*/ redrawB2(); /*982E*/ redrawB3(); /*97CC*/
    }                                       /* 9448 BRL 7F9A */
done:
    finalizeVramStrips();                   /* C0/7F9A : build tilemap-strip descriptors */
}

/* ----- representative walker: stepXpos = C0/944B (the prompt's focus 944B) -------------
 * Reads v.42 (+X step count). For each of the v.42 pixels:
 *   INX v.87 (layer-A X tile-ring index, 16-bit)
 *   advance the low nibble phase v.93; on the two tile-edge values it bumps the
 *   on-screen TILE coords v.0A (col) and v.0C (row?) and flags v.76 bit0 = "redraw".
 * The "$93==$0F" edge (prompt's special case): wrap forward, INC v.0A/v.0C, request redraw,
 * reset phase to 0xFF then +1 -> 0; the "==$07" is the half-tile (16x8) sub-edge. */
void stepXpos(void) {                        /* 944B */
    uint8_t n = v.42; if (n == 0) return;    /* 944B-944F early RTS if no +X step */
    v.66 = n;                                /* 9450 loop counter */
    do {                                     /* 9452 */
        v.87 += 1;                           /* 9452-9456 INX layer-A X ring index */
        uint8_t a = v.93;                    /* 9457 current phase */
        if (a == 0x0F) {                     /* 9459 tile boundary */
            v.0A++; v.0C++;                  /* 945D-945F bump screen tile col/row */
            v.76 |= 0x01;                    /* 9463 request redraw (axis-A) */
            a = 0xFF;                        /* 9465 (will +1 -> 0) */
        }
        if (a == 0x07) {                     /* 9467 half-tile boundary */
            v.0A++; v.0C++;                  /* 946B-946D */
            v.76 |= 0x01;                    /* 9471 */
            a = 0x07;                        /* 9473 (will +1 -> 0x08) */
        }
        v.93 = a + 1;                        /* 9475-9476 INC A; STA $93 */
    } while (--v.66 != 0);                    /* 9478-947A */
}
/* stepXneg (947D) is the mirror: reads v.41, DEX v.87, on v.93==0 -> DEC v.0A/v.0C +
 * v.77|=0x01, on ==0x08 -> DEC + v.77|=0x01; v.93 = a-1.
 * stepYpos(94DF)/stepYneg(94AD) are identical but key off v.96 phase, v.89 ring index,
 * bump v.0E/v.10, set v.74/v.75 bit0.
 * The layer-B set (950F/9545/95AF/9579) keys off v.94/v.97 phase, v.8B/v.8D ring, bumps
 * v.12/v.14 (and v.16/v.18 for the 0x47/0x48 variants) and uses the v.35 BIT #$02 gate so
 * an edge already requested this frame is not requested twice (TSB $76 #$02).
 * The layer-C set (96B7/96ED/975F/9721) keys off v.95/v.98 phase, v.8F/v.91 ring, gate
 * v.35 BIT #$04 (TSB #$04). 9721 also does INC v.FB x4 (a wide-scroll DMA budget bump);
 * 975F does DEC v.FB x4.
 * The BMI ("alt") variants (95E3/9619/9683/964D) are the WIDE-scroll mode: thresholds
 * 0x1F/0x0F instead of 0x0F/0x07, bump v.12/v.14 or v.16/v.18, request v.76/77 bit1, and
 * step the ring index v.8B/v.8D only every OTHER pixel (AND #$01 gate). */

/* ----- representative redraw dispatcher: redrawA_pos = C0/98C1 ------------------------
 * For each requested edge bit in v.75 (set by the neg walkers): JSR the matching
 * background-strip builder (these write VRAM-via-WMDATA), then advance the ring index. */
void redrawA_pos(void) {                      /* 98C1 keys off v.75 */
    if (v.75 & 0x01) { build82C5(); v.9A = (v.9A - 1) & 0x1F; }   /* 98C7 */
    if (v.75 & 0x02) { build82E5(); v.9C = (v.9C - 1) & 0x1F; }   /* 98D7 */
    if (v.75 & 0x04) { build8325(); v.9E = (v.9E - 1) & 0x1F; }   /* 98E7 */
}
/* The eight redraw routines (979B/97CC/97FD/982E/985F/9890/98C1/98F2) all share this
 * shape: test v.74/75/76/77 bits 1/2/4, call one of C0/8243..8425, then INC or DEC a
 * ring cursor (v.99/9B/9D mod 0x3F for the 0x83xx builders, v.9A/9C/9E mod 0x1F for the
 * 0x82xx builders). The builders themselves (C0/8243 etc.) set WMADDL/H ($2181/$2183),
 * load tile col/row from v.0A/0C/0E/10/12/14/16/18, set v.58/5A/5C scratch, JSR a strip
 * decompressor (7612/79CF/7D66/77E4/7BA9/7E60), and TSB a v.78/79/7A/7B "built" flag. */
wramReads: $1D42 (+X whole-pixel step count, 0..15; from 91AC) -- read at 944B
$0BC9 (abs) -- scroll/redraw-order selector; BMI = wide/alt scroll mode, BPL = normal (read 93F5, 9428)
$1D35 -- per-frame edge-request gate flags (BIT #$02 layer-B / BIT #$04 layer-C: skip re-request if already done this frame)
$1D93/$1D94/$1D95/$1D96/$1D97/$1D98 -- per-coordinate tile-phase counters (low nibble within a 16px or 32px tile); compared to edge values 0x0F/0x07/0x1F/0x0F or 0/8/0x10
$1D87/$1D89/$1D8B/$1D8D/$1D8F/$1D91 -- 16-bit VRAM/tile ring indices (INX/DEX per pixel stepped)
$1D74/$1D75/$1D76/$1D77 -- redraw-request bit scratch (read by the eight redraw dispatchers to decide which strip builder to call)
$1D0A/$1D0C/$1D0E/$1D10/$1D12/$1D14/$1D16/$1D18 -- on-screen TILE column/row coords for the four coordinate layers (read by builders C0/8243-8425 to address the strip)
$1D99/$1D9B/$1D9D -- ring cursors mod 0x3F (used by 0x83xx builders), read in redraw dispatchers
$1D58/$1D5A/$1D5C -- builder scratch (tile col-1, row, count) set inside C0/8243 etc.
$1DFB -- wide-scroll DMA/work budget counter (INC x4 at 9728, DEC x4 at 9766)
$01EB (abs, in the 9923 OBJ-priority scan that FOLLOWS this cluster -- separate routine)
$7F2000 / $0F00,X / $1100,X / $0197/$0199/$019B (abs, all in 9923 OBJ scan -- NOT this tree)
wramWrites: $1D0A/$1D0C += 1 (X+ walkers) or -=1 (X- walkers) -- screen tile col/row layer A (945D/948D etc.)
$1D0E/$1D10 += / -= 1 -- screen tile col/row layer A Y (94BF/94FD)
$1D93/$1D94/$1D95/$1D96/$1D97/$1D98 = phase+1 or phase-1 -- per-pixel tile-phase advance

$1D66 = v.42 (944B stores the +X step count into $1D66 as the loop seed BEFORE counting -- note: this is the SAME byte the prop-fetch later uses as tentative-pos-low; here it is reused as a transient loop counter, so $1D66 is clobbered by this tree)
$1D87 etc. INX/DEX, and $1D66 = loop counter (transient, overwritten each walker via STA $66 / DEC $66)
$1D78/$1D79/$1D7A/$1D7B = 0 then TSB bits -- strip-built flags (9420-9426; set inside builders via TSB $78/$7A)
$2181/$2183 (WMADDL/WMADDH, PPU) and WMDATA -- written by the strip builders C0/8243-8425 (VRAM/WRAM transfer setup)
uncertainties: BIGGEST: the prompt framed 93E1 as 'position-integration + collision-apply (calls 9C5C / prop-fetch / writes $1D62/$1D64)'. The trace (boot_trace_play.txt line 660-757, one full pass of the tree) shows it does NONE of that: it only INC/DEC's screen-coord/ring bytes and the player was stationary so every walker early-RTS'd. 9C5C, 9AA1, 9AC8, 9D54 do NOT appear anywhere in boot_trace_play.txt (grep count 0). So either (a) 93E1 is purely the camera/sprite-screen-coord + tilemap-strip-redraw scheduler and the real $1D62/$1D64+collision path is elsewhere in the C0/881E body that this trace never exercised, or (b) collision IS reached only on a frame where step counts are nonzero, via a sub-path I have not seen execute. The verifier MUST capture a MOVING-player frame trace (walk into a wall) and re-grep for 9C5C/9AA1 to settle which. My strong read from the static decode is (a): every leaf JSR target here resolves to a VRAM/strip builder (C0/8243-8425 -> $2181/$2183 + strip decompressors), not to the collision core.

Exact semantic of $1D0A/$1D0C vs $1D0E/$1D10 vs $1D12/$1D14 vs $1D16/$1D18: I label them 'four coordinate layers' (likely BG1/BG2 scroll + two sprite/window coords) because the builders address four distinct VRAM strip regions ($C800/$D000/$D800 + $C880/$D080/$D880). The precise mapping of each pair to a specific PPU scroll register / sprite needs confirmation from the builder targets ($7612/$79CF/$7D66/$77E4/$7BA9/$7E60), which I did not fully decode.

$1D66 reuse: 944B does STA $66 (the +X step count) as a loop counter and DEC $66. Elsewhere in the project $1D66 is documented as 'tentative next position low'. Confirm the call ordering guarantees the prop-fetch (which reads $1D66) runs BEFORE this tree, otherwise $1D66 is clobbered. (In the C0/881E call order the integration+collision precedes the redraw; this tree being the redraw stage is consistent with $1D66 being free to reuse here.)

$0BC9 meaning: inferred to be the scroll-mode / redraw-order selector (BMI picks wider 0x1F/0x0F tile thresholds and half-rate ring stepping = a 32px wide-scroll layer mode). Not cross-referenced in any note; pin it from where $0BC9 is written.

$1D35 gate bits: I read BIT #$02 (layer-B) and BIT #$04 (layer-C) as 'edge already requested this frame, do not double-request'. The producer of $1D35 (who sets bits 1/2/4) is upstream and not decoded here.

Number of integration sub-passes per frame: the X/Y/B/C step loops are ONE pass each (the early-RTS makes the per-pixel loop run 0..15 times). Per frame the tree runs: 4 layer-A walkers + 4 layer-B walkers + 4 layer-C walkers = 12 coordinate walkers, then 4 redraw dispatchers, then BRL 7F9A. So ONE integration sub-pass per direction per coordinate-layer per frame; each sub-pass iterates per-whole-pixel of that direction's step count. There is NO multi-iteration outer loop. (If the verifier expected N collision sub-passes for a multi-pixel move, those would be in the SEPARATE collision path, not here.)

The routine at C0/9923 (immediately after this cluster) is a DIFFERENT routine (an OBJ-priority/visibility scan over actors $1100,X reading $0197/$0199/$019B and $7F2000); it is reached by its own JSR, not by fall-through from 9922, and is out of scope for this tree.
